latch.mechanism: over-centre toggle (crank r 8.0, link 20, 4 deg past dead centre onto a stop) pulling the keyhole jaw through a 4-disc A20 cartridge; arm 18 mm with a D10 roller; closing by two constant-force springs; opened only by the dock lift bar

pins.bearing: drawn-cup needle roller bearing on a D4 hardened ground pin (HK0408 class, bought; UNVERIFIED part) at the crank pivot and the crank pin; the cartridge pin rides in the jaw (plain)

closing_spring.name: constant-force spring (coiled stainless strip on a drum), 46 N class, 10 mm strip, drum about D16 (catalogue class, UNVERIFIED part), two per carriage, one each side of the arm

holding.locked_against_opening: a pull on the tool pushes the jaw (+Y), which pulls the link and drives the crank harder onto its over-centre stop: it cannot open, whatever the pull, until a part yields
holding.beyond_preload: above the preload the balls lift and the stack compresses further; at the stack's catalogue limit (75 % of flat, +0.46 mm) the stud carries 1521 N; flat at 1976 N; then the load passes into the hardened D4 pins (double shear, far above)
holding.power_loss: nothing on the latch is powered; the dock lift is a lead screw (self-locking), so a power cut anywhere leaves the latch as it was: closed everywhere except inside a bay with the tool already on the bay pins

release.what: dock lift bar pushing the roller up: spring + toggle through dead centre + pin friction; the stack energy is given back as the toggle passes centre

relatch.what: the constant-force springs close the toggle and compresses the stack when the bar is lowered with the stud seated

wear_points: jaw flank / stud cone: one sliding stroke under about 0.8 kN per latch: both hardened (jaw 58 HRC, bought knob), grease; inspect at 1,000 exchanges (CT-5) for galling
toggle pins in DU-class bushings: replace the bushings if the latch switch window drifts
roller on the bar pad: rolling, hardened pad
balls and vee seats: Hertz contact (coupling.hertz_working); inspect after any crash
dock lift nut (anti-backlash, POM): 2 strokes per exchange

sensing.detects: an open or half-open jaw; a stud cone 0.12 mm or more off its nominal height (a 0.3 mm shim under the +X ball lowers the stud 0.18 mm: CLOSED-EMPTY with a code = HOLD); NOT detected: a shim under one of the two -X balls (stud moves 0.06 mm, inside the knob tolerance): CT-4 measures which shims the switch catches
sensing.switches: sealed subminiature switch with pin plunger and factory lead (D2SW-P class, UNVERIFIED part): operating-point repeatability <= 0.02 mm class, over-travel >= 0.8 mm (the LOCK switch is driven 0.66 mm past its operating point when the jaw closes empty: PURCHASE CONDITION)
sensing.set: each switch is moved on its slotted holes until it just operates with the stated feeler between the flag and the jaw stop face (build step 5)

latch.z_only_verdict: NOT POSSIBLE with the Z axis alone, whatever the force: (1) the latch may only open once the tool rests on the bay pins, and then the carriage cannot move further down, so a fixed post has no motion to work with; opening it earlier drops the tool through the last millimetres; (2) a drop-off and a pick-up are the same Z motion at the same bay, so a fixed post cannot leave the tool in one case and take it in the other (revision L's post had this fault: rising after a drop-off its spring re-closed the jaw on the cone and lifted the tool again).  The force alone would now pass (z_only_comparison) because of the toggle.

guards: TOOLS-UP chain: XY motion only with all three Z-up switches made (carriage A, B, gripper), as now with three axes

TOOL PRESENT AND LOCKED: before any XY move each carriage reads either (code 0000 AND latch closed-empty) or (code == expected AND latch switch in window); any other combination = HOLD, Z stays where it is
HALF-LOCK: code present + latch out of window = HOLD; never move XY; the run asks for a person
DROPPED TOOL: code goes to 0000 or latch leaves the window while not in a bay = emergency stop of XY, Z hold
WRONG TOOL: code != planner's expected tool for that bay/carriage = HOLD before leaving the bay
BAY CHECK: after a drop-off the bay switch must close; after a pick-up it must open; otherwise HOLD
POWER-UP: read both codes and latches before homing; a tool on a carriage is homed with Z up only (no Z-down homing), and its nozzle position is re-checked at the tip gate before any work
TIP CHECK PER TOOL: after every pick-up the tip gate checks presence and VC-2 the tip length (tip type) for that tool
EJECT: the eject over-travel is allowed only for a carriage whose code says a tool with tips is fitted; the fixed finger enters the bracket hole only above s = 0

LATCH OPEN only inside a dock bay, by the dock lift: bar UP only with a carriage at a bay centre at the dock stroke and either the bay switch made (drop-off) or Hall code 0000 (pick-up); X/Y never move unless the bar home switch is made

PUSHER: homes UP to its RETRACTED switch at <= 0.5 A and <= 2 mm/s; it must never be driven into the actuator's internal end stop above 0.57 A (maker's limit for this thread); soft limits 0.5 .. 37.5 mm
safety.power_loss: over-centre latch held by geometry (needs no power, no spring) and closed by two constant-force springs: a tool cannot drop; the dock lift is a lead screw and stays where it is; Z screws self-locking; pusher self-locking

drop_off (carriage C carrying tool T to: 1 X/Y over bay k at the dock row (no tips), bar DOWN (home switch made); Z down to the seat stroke L_DOCK_S: the cradle lugs land on the bay pins; bay switch k must close

2 bar UP by the roller rise (+3 mm approach) at 5 mm/s: the roller is lifted, the toggle passes dead centre, the stack relaxes, the jaw opens; the bar OPEN-height switch must be made and the latch must read NOT CLOSED (both switches off)
3 Z up 13 mm and bar up 13 mm together, in 1 mm steps (bar first): the stud head leaves the jaw downwards with the jaw held open
4 bar DOWN to home: the spring closes the empty jaw (latch reads CLOSED-EMPTY: LOCK and EMPTY switches made); Hall code must read 0000

5 Z up to s 0 (single drop-off) or to the in-row stroke IN_ROW_S (exchange: the empty carriage moves along the row to the pick-up bay at that stroke, the other carriage and the gripper at s 0); leave the dock row at its right end
pick_up (empty carriage C takes tool T f: 1 X/Y over bay k (no tips), bar DOWN; Z down to L_DOCK_S - 13 (the stud head is 0.5 mm below the jaw)
2 bar UP by the roller rise + 3 + 13 mm: the jaw opens
3 Z down 13 mm and bar down 13 mm together, in 1 mm steps (Z first): the balls seat on the vee seats, the stud head passes up through the open keyhole

4 bar DOWN to home at 5 mm/s: the spring closes the toggle, the jaw draws the stud up through the cone and the stack takes the preload; latch must read LOCKED (LOCK switch made, EMPTY not); Hall code must equal T
5 Z up: the tool leaves the bay pins (bay switch k must open); tip-gate nozzle check before work
guards (firmware): bar UP only with a carriage at a bay centre (X within 0.5 mm), Z at the stroke of step 1, and either bay switch k made (drop-off) or Hall code 0000 on that carriage (pick-up); otherwise refuse
the bar never moves while either carriage's X/Y moves; X/Y never move unless the bar home switch is made
a latch switch outside its expected state after any step = HOLD, Z where it is

tests.FIRST - CT-0a latch release force: the rig carriage with the LTG-1 latch, a tool latched on a seated two-bay dock; the dock lift pushes the roller through the 500 N button cell under the pad: log force vs bar stroke; pass: peak <= lift thrust / 1.5 and within 20 % of the calculated profile (head report coupling.latch.table)
tests.FIRST - CT-0b re-latch force and preload: bar lowered slowly with the stud seated: the springs must close the toggle 100 of 100 times with 0.67 x spring force (a third of the springs' force taken off by a hanging weight); preload measured with PLF-L and the S-cell (separation at the tool plate edge) for each of 6 knobs: pass >= 520 N
tests.FIRST - CT-1 repeatability, 1,000 exchan: two indicators (X, Y) on magnetic bases touch the ground D6 pin held on the nozzle (NRP-L); exchange tool in/out of the two-bay dock with the dock lift; pass <= 0.10 mm 3 sigma at the nozzle
tests.FIRST - CT-0c comb entry with real tips: one TPK-S group (S E S) cut for the rig M300's measured nozzle row: 500 park/re-pick cycles of real p300 tips in random order: no strike, no collar left out of its pocket, no tip left on a strip
tests.FIRST - CT-0d pusher force at 0.7 A: LGA35 at 0.7 A, 24 V, 2 / 5 / 8 mm/s against the 200 N button cell with the die spring in series in the pusher line: pass >= 120 N at 5 mm/s (80 N x 1.5) without lost steps; also log the homing stall current (<= 0.57 A)
tests.CT-2 added deflection at 120 / 150 N: LJF-L pushes the nozzle pin sideways through the 500 N S-cell; pass <= 0.05 mm
tests.CT-3 no lift-off at 2 x the working forc: PLF-L pulls the tool plate down through the S-cell to 2 x eject/strip force; separation < 0.005 mm
tests.CT-4 power-off pull and half-locks: motor power off, pull at 2 x; shim under one ball, wrong bay, debris, a constant-force spring removed: the latch must never read LOCKED with a bad seat it can detect (latch.SENSE: stud 0.12 mm or more off), and the tool never drops; record which shims read CLOSED-EMPTY / NOT CLOSED
tests.CT-SYR syringe return spring: 10 mL syringe with the 1.5 x 20 x 75 return spring: plunger seal friction (pull-out force at 1 mm/s, wet), the plunger follows the pusher up 100 of 100 refills at 5 mm/s; pass: spring force out / measured friction + valve >= 1.5
tests.CT-5 3,000 exchanges: automatic cycling between the two bays with the dock lift; no undetected failure, <= 1 detected per 1,000
tests.CT-6 pipetting after exchange: gravimetric, S10 and M300, against the same pipette bolted directly
tests.CT-7 force switch through the push-rod: load cell under the nozzle: trip within 15 % of the cradle's set force
tests.CT-8 tool code: Hall switches against 1,000 insertions: no misread
tests.CT-9 real forces: eight-tip pick-up, comb strip, ejector, 1,000 uL plunger

assembly_steps_and_gauges: 1 vee seats: screw the three bought hardened vee seats into their bracket pockets (2 x M3 each) with the grooves pointing at the drilled centre mark; alignment needed +/-1 deg, +/-0.2 mm: checked by eye against the scribed radial line and with calipers to the centre mark (a kinematic coupling repeats on its contacts, not its placement)

2 tooling balls: screw the three bought shank balls into the tool plate until each shoulder seats on its spot face (finger-tight + thread locker); check: the three ball tops within 0.03 mm, dial indicator on a magnetic base, plate face down on a flat surface
3 retention knob: screw the bought knob to its shoulder (torque per its sheet); nothing to set

4 latch: fit jaw, 3-disc cartridge (discs unloaded at assembly: no compression fixture), link, crank and arm on the needle-bearing pins, the two constant-force springs (hook on, no tool); with a tool latched, adjust the cartridge nut until a 0.50 mm feeler enters the cartridge gap window and a 0.60 mm feeler does not (stack compression 0.55 mm); lock the nut

5 latch switches: with a tool latched and a 0.12 mm feeler between the flag and the LOCK switch's plunger, move the LOCK switch on its slots until it just operates; with no tool, the flag closed, set the EMPTY switch the same way 0.42 mm (0.54 - 0.12) short of the flag (feelers 0.40 / 0.45 bracket it); check: tool latched reads LOCKED (4.9 k at the ladder), no tool CLOSED-EMPTY (2.3 k), bar up NOT CLOSED (23 k); with a 0.3 mm feeler under the +X ball it must not read LOCKED (CT-4 at build)
6 bracket to the Z carriage: 4 x M5 with an engineer's square against the carriage plate: coupling plane square within 0.1 mm over 100 mm, checked with a 0.10 mm feeler under the square
7 per-tool offset: at commissioning, measure each tool's nozzle position at the tip gate / head camera and store it (no gauge)
8 dock lift: bar level within 0.5 mm over the row (spirit level and calipers from the dock base); home switch flag set so the pads stand 3 +/- 0.5 mm under a locked roller (feeler stack)
dedicated gauges: none (was GG-L1..GG-L5); ordinary tools: feeler gauges, dial indicator on a magnetic base, calipers, square, level
